Accepts a batch of telemetry events from CLI tools and AI agents.
Events are validated, timestamped, and stored in the app's event stream.

**Authentication:** API key (`axk_...`) in `Authorization: Bearer` header.
No JWT required — this endpoint is designed for embedding in open-source CLIs.

**Collection controls:** If the app has `collection_enabled: false`, events are
accepted but silently dropped (returns `{"status": 1, "accepted": 0}`).

params.name: team_id
params.description: Team ID to list apps for. Must be a valid `team_` prefixed ID.

items.docs:
Returns all AgentX applications registered to the specified team.
API keys are never included in list responses.

The caller must be an active member of the specified team.

Creates a new AgentX application and returns the API key.

**The API key is shown only once in this response.** It is not retrievable
later via the GET endpoint. To obtain a new key, delete the app and recreate it.

The caller must be an active member of the specified team.

**Default metadata:** `rate_limit: 1000/min`, `burst_limit: 5000/min`, `monthly_quota: 10M events`.

Returns application details including metadata and settings.
The API key is **not** included — it is only shown once at creation time.

Requires JWT authentication and team membership.

Permanently deletes the application and invalidates its API key.
Any subsequent capture requests using this key will fail with 401.

**This action is irreversible.** All associated event data remains in storage
but is no longer queryable through the dashboard.

Updates collection control settings for the app.

- **`collection_enabled`**: When `false`, the capture endpoint accepts events
  but drops them immediately — zero server-side resources consumed.
- **`sample_rate`**: Controls what fraction of events are stored (0.0 to 1.0).
  Events are randomly sampled before database insertion. Set to `1.0` to keep
  all events, or lower to reduce storage for high-volume apps.

Returns events in the last 24 hours. Does not accept date range parameters.

params.name: tz
params.description: IANA timezone for time series bucketing. Defaults to UTC.

items.docs:
Returns aggregate statistics for the specified date range: total events,
unique users, friction event count, friction rate, and latest client version.

Returns time-bucketed event counts grouped by event name.
Buckets are hourly for ranges <= 7 days, daily for longer ranges.

params.name: metrics
params.description: Comma-separated list of metric sections to include. Omit to include all.

items.docs:
Returns comprehensive friction analysis with selective metric loading.
Use the `metrics` parameter to request only the sections you need — each
metric is fetched concurrently for optimal performance.

**Available metrics:** `time_series`, `by_actor`, `by_tool`,
`top_unknown_commands`, `agent_stats`, `client_versions`, `hotspots`,
`recent_events`.

When `compare=true`, includes a previous-period comparison for trend analysis.

Returns the top 50 commands by usage count with percentage distribution.
Command names are extracted from `properties->>'command'` in events.

Returns event counts grouped by actor and agent type.
Labels are formatted as `{actor}/{agent_type}` (e.g., `agent/copilot`).

Returns daily event counts grouped by client library version
(`properties->>'$lib_version'`). Useful for tracking version adoption curves.

params.name: start_date
params.description: Start of date range (ISO 8601 date or datetime). Defaults to 7 days ago.

params.name: end_date
params.description: End of date range (ISO 8601 date or datetime). Defaults to now.

items.docs:
Returns daily active user counts. Users are identified by
`COALESCE(properties->>'$user_id', distinct_id)`.

Streams all friction events for the date range as a CSV download.

**Columns:** `ts`, `event`, `distinct_id`, `kind`, `actor`, `agent_type`,
`command`, `subcommand`, `input`, `error_msg`, `suggestion`, `lib_version`,
`path_bucket`, `user_id`.
